On June 12, **SpaceX** (NASDAQ: SPCX) completed the largest initial public offering (IPO) in history, raising about $75 billion at a valuation of about $1.75 trillion -- more than double the size of any stock market debut before it. SpaceX went public in the middle of a wave of artificial intelligence (AI) spending unlike anything the market has seen, with the four biggest technology companies alone on track to pour about $725 billion into capital expenditures (much of it on data centers and chips this year) -- up about 77% from last year. To some investors, a record listing landing on top of all that spending looks like the kind of enthusiasm that shows up near market tops. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. The *Motley Fool Stock Advisor* analyst team just identified what they believe are the **10 best stocks** for investors to buy now… and Alphabet wasn’t one of them.

items.title: The AI Startup Funding Boom Is Not A Global Phenomenon
items.snippet: # The AI Startup Funding Boom Is Not A Global Phenomenon. The flood of AI-focuse...
items.raw_snippet: # The AI Startup Funding Boom Is Not A Global Phenomenon. The flood of AI-focused funding has pushed global startup investment to record levels this year. So far in 2026, U.S. companies have pulled in nearly 80% of global seed- through growth-stage financing, per Crunchbase data. That’s a sharp divergence from the years leading up to the AI boom, when American companies typically secured less than half of all investment. The U.S. share of artificial intelligence-related investment is even greater. So far this year, nearly 88% of AI-related startup funding, or $319 billion, went to U.S.-headquartered companies, per Crunchbase data. Although no other country comes close to the U.S. for startup funding, a few of the larger technology investment hubs are seeing year-over-year gains. Now that more than three-fourths of startup funding is going to U.S. companies, it seems timely to note that the country is home to only a little over 4% of the global population.

items.raw_snippet: ##### Europe & Africa. ##### Middle East. #### Select your region and language. ##### Europe, Middle East, & Africa. ##### Hiring Process. ###### Your Previous Searches. Content added to saved items. By Mark Krafft, Evren Sungur, and Praveen Bhardwaj. When organizations centralize work into shared services, often coupled with offshoring, they create conditions that make both process improvement and AI more viable:. Conventional wisdom cautions "Don't outsource your mess for less." In theory, companies should standardize first, then move the work. In practice, fixing processes in a decentralized structure is slow and politically complex. Immediate savings create economic headroom, central visibility exposes variation, and governance becomes clearer. items.title: SaaS Pricing Shift: How to Negotiate AI-Driven Renewals
items.snippet: Finance leaders collaborate in a modern boardroom, analyzing the impact of AI-dr...
items.raw_snippet: Finance leaders collaborate in a modern boardroom, analyzing the impact of AI-driven software renewals. ## The CFO's 2026 AI Renewal Playbook: Surviving the AI Tax at Contract Time. The line item on the 2026 software renewal quote that was not present in previous years—an artificial intelligence pricing uplift ranging from 20 to 37 percent—is not a rounding error. The software-as-a-service industry is currently undergoing a fundamental transformation, abandoning predictable, seat-based subscription models in favor of dynamic, usage- and outcome-based frameworks driven by the integration of autonomous agentic capabilities. For financial leaders, procurement teams, and chief technology officers evaluating these rapidly approaching renewals, the introductory trial-month expenditure is rarely a reliable indicator of the ultimate financial burden when projected over a thirty-six-month operational scale. This comprehensive research report provides a robust, data-driven framework for finance and technology executives to evaluate AI pricing uplifts, decode shifting SaaS monetization strategies, implement protective contract mechanisms, and determine the optimal inflection point for replacing external vendor dependencies with custom software solutions.

The term "Advisory Committee" means the National Artificial Intelligence Advisory Committee established under section 9414(a) of this title. The term "agency head" means the head of any Executive agency (as defined in section 105 of title 5). The term "Initiative" means the National Artificial Intelligence Initiative established under section 9411(a) of this title. The term "Initiative Office" means the National Artificial Intelligence Initiative Office established under section 9412(a) of this title. (a) Within 180 days of this order [Jan. 23, 2025], the Assistant to the President for Science and Technology (APST), the Special Advisor for AI and Crypto, and the Assistant to the President for National Security Affairs (APNSA), in coordination with the Assistant to the President for Economic Policy, the Assistant to the President for Domestic Policy, the Director of the Office of Management and Budget (OMB Director), and the heads of such executive departments and agencies (agencies) as the APST and APNSA deem relevant, shall develop and submit to the President an action plan to achieve the policy set forth in section 2 of this order.
